name: R01 fold: a gap that CONTAINS a space, not one that starts with it
why: a tab then a blank is two deep (the fold takes a blank off only a gap that STARTS with one): the behaviour row `#|<tab><blank>fig-cap` then `#|<blank><blank>label`

name: R02 fold: the folded indent capped at 2
why: gaps of 4 and 5 blanks are 3 and 4 deep, not both 2: the behaviour row with those gaps

name: R03 fold: a tab counts as 8 columns
why: a tab and two blanks are both one deep: the behaviour row `#|<tab>fig-cap` then `#|<blank><blank>label`

name: R04 compare: only a depth that differs by exactly 1 is skipped
why: a key two columns deeper is skipped: the behaviour row `#| fig-cap` then `#|<3 blanks>label`

name: R05 compare: depths of the same parity are the same depth
why: the same behaviour row: a depth that differs by 2 is a different depth

name: R06 call site: the prefix capped at its last 4,096 characters
why: a different cure for the quadratic that changes the answer for gaps over 4,096: the behaviour rows with gaps of 5,000 and 6,000 blanks on two option lines (different depths, so no label) and of 5,000 and 5,000 (equal, so the label)

name: R07 trailingBlanks: the old search below 40,000 characters, the scan above
why: answers identically but costs 1 s at 39,990 blanks; the near-miss rows now time a run of 20,000 as well (the old search takes 240 ms there, the limit is 100)

name: R08 trailingBlanks: a hand-rolled scan that also takes U+2003 (EM SPACE)
why: the code-unit row: every UTF-16 code unit as the last character, after a blank, before a blank

name: R09 trailingBlanks: a hand-rolled scan that also takes U+200B (ZERO WIDTH SPACE)
why: the code-unit row

name: R10 trailingBlanks: a hand-rolled scan that also takes U+1680 (OGHAM SPACE MARK)
why: the code-unit row

name: R11 trimEndBlanks: a space, a tab or U+2003 trimmed
why: killed by trim-end-blanks.test.ts before; the code-unit row now kills it through trailingBlanks as well

name: R12 equivalence file: the near-miss clock limit is 100,000 ms
why: with a limit of 100 s the old search (1.5 s at 50,000 blanks) passes the near-miss rows, so R-C01 is visible only in the other file: the sentinel row pins the limit

name: R13 equivalence file: the million-blank size never runs
why: a cap at 999,999 survives without the million: the sentinel row pins the sizes

name: R14 equivalence file: the near-miss sizes are small
why: at 1,000 blanks the old search is fast: the sentinel row pins the sizes

name: R15 equivalence file: the trailing run is 2,000 blanks
why: the sentinel row pins the length

name: R16 equivalence file: U+2029 replaced by a letter in the second alphabet
why: a letter in place of a character moves neither the string count nor the answered count: the sentinel row pins the alphabets by code point

name: R17 equivalence file: the vertical tab replaced by a letter in the third alphabet
why: the sentinel row pins the alphabets by code point

name: E01 helper: substring instead of slice
why: substring(i) and slice(i) agree for 0 <= i <= length: equivalent

name: E02 helper: || undefined
why: slice(undefined) is slice(0): equivalent

name: E03 helper: lookbehind-anchored search (a linear regex cure)
why: a lookbehind-anchored regular expression is another LINEAR spelling with identical answers: compared on 2,046,952 strings over three alphabets with none different (the helper at 1,000,000 blanks: 4.7 ms)

name: E04 helper: guard for a text that ends in a space or a tab
why: the run is empty exactly when the text ends in neither a space nor a tab: equivalent

name: E05 helper: guard for the empty text
why: the empty text has an empty run: equivalent

name: E06 helper: guard when nothing was trimmed
to:
const kept = trimEndBlanks(text).length;
  return kept === text.length ? "" : text.slice(kept);
why: nothing trimmed means an empty run: equivalent

name: E07 helper: the run capped at 1,000,000 (the longest the tests build)
why: the run capped at 1,000,000: the boundary of the longest run any row builds, so no finite row kills it (a cap at 999,999 is killed, by the run-is-the-gap row)

name: E08 fold: replace(/^ /) length
why: replace(/^ /, '').length is the same fold: equivalent (8,191 gaps compared)

name: E09 fold: Math.max(gap.length - 1, 0)
why: a gap that starts with a space has length >= 1, so Math.max(.., 0) changes nothing: equivalent

name: E10 base: also set on the first option line
why: the first option line that reaches the fold is the first real key, where baseIndent is still null: equivalent

name: E11 site: the prefix cut one character in at the start
why: the prefix is the opener, [ \t]*, a pipe and the gap, and no opener holds a blank, so a prefix cut one character in still ends in the same run: equivalent (599,186 real option lines compared)

name: E12 site: the end taken from the key's end column and length
why: keyToken is lineText.slice(startCol, endCol): equivalent

name: E13 site: raw line sliced from the removed indent
why: lineText is rawLine.slice(removed): equivalent

name: E14 site: the inline form (slice from trimEndBlanks)
why: the helper written inline: equivalent

name: E15 site: the line before the key's first character, minus the comment run
why: the strip touches only leading hashes and the run is trailing: equivalent

name: E16 site: trimEnd() where the call site reads the prefix
to:
const prefix = lineText.slice(0, keySlot.startCol);
      const gap = prefix.slice(prefix.trimEnd().length);
why: the prefix is comment characters, [ \t]*, a pipe and [ \t]*, so it ends in blanks and trimEnd() strips the same run: equivalent

name: E17 trimEndBlanks: end >= 0 (reads charCodeAt(-1) = NaN)
why: trimEndBlanks reading charCodeAt(-1), which is NaN and equals neither blank: equivalent
